cells.tense: The fire is lit, the direction is clear, and the words are moving now.
cells.act: think it through to its sharp point
cells.ask: Take one idea you've been carrying loosely and work it down to the hard edge. Then hand the finished version to somebody who will use it. No pitch — just the clean thought.
cells.core:
There's a shape under things that you can name, and lately you've been naming it without dressing it up. Not just the idea — how it moves, what it asks for, where it's headed. When someone takes fire from you, it's because you handed them the plain version and stood back. That hasn't been effort. It's been what you do, and it doesn't need guarding or repeating.
What wants doing is smaller than it sounds. You have ideas sitting in loose form — half-drawn, mentioned once, on a list. Pick one this week and work it to the hard edge, don't round it off, and hand it to somebody who will actually use it. Not a pitch. The finished thought, in your own order, clean enough that they can carry it themselves.
cells.sheetLine: You see the pattern and can say it plainly now.
cells.verb: Turning inner fire into outward expression, radiating confidence and sparking it in others.
cells.place: Where patterns are seen stripped of everything literal, pure mechanism beneath the surface.

cells.tense: The next move is being written before the current one has landed.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Sit beside somebody who's just meeting the idea you're surest of. Ask the question whose answer you don't hold, and leave whatever comes back where it lands.
cells.core:
Where the spark lives, the timing has slipped. The next version gets sketched before the current one has finished finding out what it is, and the anticipation reads as pressure from outside — people feel carried and managed at once. The confidence earned by having built something gets spent on the next build before the first is allowed to stand. A hot engine in a cold week. Not a flaw, a timing error.
The pull back is not to damp the fire, it's to spend one honest hour as a student of something. Take the idea you're surest of and sit beside somebody just meeting it. Ask a question whose answer you don't already hold, and leave their answer standing without correction. The thing you built is allowed to finish completing itself while you're not watching it.
cells.sheetLine: You're building the next thing before the last one finishes.
cells.verb: Turning inner fire into outward expression, radiating confidence and sparking it in others.
cells.place: Where patterns are seen stripped of everything literal, pure mechanism beneath the surface.

cells.tense: The version of this that used to move is standing still at a door already closed behind it.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Look after something ordinary you own — a plant, a shelf, a pot — twice this week, giving it what it actually asks for rather than what you meant to give.
cells.core:
The confidence went somewhere and hasn't come back out. You can still tell when a shape is real and when it's just noise, but the part that put it in front of people has stepped back. The door behind you is clearer than the one ahead, and that is simply where you're standing. Nothing about it needs settling tonight.
The way forward isn't through the big idea. It's through something small and material, with a need that doesn't care whether you're inspired. Water it, fix it, feed it, twice this week. Not to feel better — to remember what direction through your hands is like when it isn't a performance. When the thing answers back, the confidence has somewhere to land that isn't an argument.
cells.sheetLine: You still see the pattern. Putting it in front of people has stepped back.
cells.verb: Turning inner fire into outward expression, radiating confidence and sparking it in others.
cells.place: Where patterns are seen stripped of everything literal, pure mechanism beneath the surface.

cells.tense: The pattern is walked in your own steps and credited to nobody around you.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Catch one move you made this week that changed a decision, and set it in a single line under your own name. What you saw, what you did, that it was yours. Then leave it.
cells.core:
You see the shape under things and you act on it, and the story you tell is that it just happened, or someone else said it first, or it was obvious. It isn't. You are the one walking through the pattern and choosing where it goes, and your telling of it hasn't caught up. Other people are standing on the decisions you made and skipping the part where you made them.
This week, name one move in one line and put your name under it. Not a diary entry. One sentence: the pattern you saw, the move you made, and that it was yours. Then leave it be. The point isn't credit, it's that the fire is coming from somewhere, and that somewhere has a pen.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern is walked in your steps and signed in your hand.
cells.verb: Turning inner fire into outward expression, radiating confidence and sparking it in others.
cells.place: Where patterns are seen stripped of everything literal, pure mechanism beneath the surface.

attempts.check: The record supports the person's confidence as observable behaviour, but nothing here says it is rewarded or lands well; the likely objection is that this is exactly who they are, and if nothing is misfiring, no reading is needed. The asks survive that: each names one small act the person can try and verify for themselves, and the Too Much ask is only ever 'you don't have to explain the idea, just build a piece of it' — not 'do less'. The sentence that serves me is the poetic one about the fire outrunning the fireplace; the plain one is 'there's a pattern you're pointing at that no one else can see yet.'
